title: Japan’s MMX Probe Sets Off for Mars’s Moon Phobos
paragraphs: A Japanese space machine called MMX started its journey to Mars on 20 October 2026. A big H3 rocket carried it into space from the Tanegashima Space Center in Japan.

MMX will study Phobos, one of the two small moons of Mars. Scientists still do not know how Phobos and its sister moon, Deimos, were made. To find out, MMX will land on Phobos and take a small piece of the surface.

The trip will take a long time. MMX should reach Mars in August 2027, and it will land on Phobos in 2030. The piece of Phobos should arrive on Earth in 2031. The mission is led by Japan, but NASA, France, Germany and Europe are helping.

questions.q: Where did the H3 rocket take off?
questions.a: From the Tanegashima Space Center in Japan.

questions.q: What will MMX take from Phobos?
questions.a: A small piece of the surface.
